name: Xcode compilation cache (COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING, Xcode 26)
baseline: xcodebuild clean build with no cache
verdict_reason: With a populated cache, clean builds were 18-77% faster across four real projects in Tuist's measurements. Apple publishes no figure of its own. The size of the win depends heavily on project structure: SwiftPM-heavy projects gained least because parts of package builds are not cacheable yet.
tier_reason: Public benchmark repository with hyperfine runs; the post names Namespace M4 Pro runners and Xcode 26.0.1, and the benchmarker is independent of Apple.
claimed_speedup: Local cache: Wikipedia 24%, Pocket Casts 36%, Tuist CLI 77% shorter clean builds; remote cache: 18%, 20% and 53%; Mastodon 19% (local) and 30% (remote) with SwiftPM, 55% and 69% as a Tuist-generated project. Wikipedia 69.328 s to 53.072 s and Pocket Casts 168.073 s to 108.634 s with the local cache
workload: Clean builds with a pre-populated local or remote compilation cache of Wikipedia iOS, Pocket Casts iOS, Mastodon iOS and the Tuist CLI, 3-5 runs each
install: built into Xcode 26+; set COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING = YES
one_liner: Xcode 26's opt-in content-addressed compilation cache; Tuist measured 18-77% shorter clean builds once the cache is warm.
how_it_is_fast: Xcode 26 keys each compilation on its inputs in an action cache and stores outputs in content-addressable storage, the same model Bazel and Gradle use. When the key matches, the compiler output is reused instead of recompiled. Xcode still plans and runs the rest of the build around those cache hits.
use_it_when: Xcode 26+ projects with frequent clean builds, branch switches or derived-data wipes
Projects whose code lives in Xcode targets rather than Swift packages
skip_it_when: SwiftPM-heavy projects expecting large gains: package builds have uncacheable steps
Teams without a remote cache server, who only get the local cache
caveats: Measured by Tuist, which sells a remote cache server for this feature
Only 3-5 runs per configuration on CI runners
Measured on Xcode 26.0.1, the first release of the feature; later Xcode versions may differ
tradeoffs: Remote caching needs a server that speaks Xcode's cache protocol
Disk usage for the local CAS
Opt-in build setting; not on by default

evidence.quote: For Wikipedia, the build time was reduced by 24% when using the local cache (simulating clean builds with local compilation cache already populated) and by 18% when using the remote cache (simulating clean builds with remote, not local, compilation cache already populated). For Pocket Casts, the build times were reduced by 36% for the local cache and by 20% for the remote cache.
We've observed the biggest improvement in build times for Tuist CLI, where the build time was reduced by 77% when using the local cache and by 53% when using the remote cache.

Whereas building Mastodon with the local cache and the remote cache with the default SwiftPM integration improved the build by 19% and 30%, respectively, the improvements were 55% and 69% for the Mastodon project generated with Tuist.
M4 Pro runners on 20th and 21st October 2025 using Xcode 26.0.1.
